own_solution.law: Steady rigid-body rotation gives dz/dr = omega²r/g. Conservation of liquid volume gives h_axis = h_initial - omega²R²/(4g) = 0.30 - 100(0.15)²/(4 × 9.8). With upward platform acceleration a, replace g by g+a.
assumptions: The platform has no vertical acceleration in the base scenario.
The liquid has reached steady rigid-body rotation.
The free surface is at uniform atmospheric pressure.
The tank retains all its liquid, and the bottom remains covered.

TE262.regime: The wall must exceed the maximum free-surface height, h_wall = 0.30 + omega²R²/(4g) = 0.3573979592 m; the stated height of 0.70 m prevents spilling.

T499A.regime: The wall must exceed the maximum free-surface height, h_wall = 0.3573979592 m; the stated height of 0.70 m prevents spilling.

defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: The acceleration variants do not consistently state the same number: T2913 and T3820 use the unspecified phrase 'a few metres per second squared', whereas TAF0F and T80DF respectively specify 3.9 m/s².

notes: The physics yields a unique answer under the ordinary reading of the description; the invalid verdict concerns the required numerical matching of sentence variants. Density cancels between the radial and vertical pressure-gradient equations. The goods lift has no stated mechanical connection to the tank, and acceleration confined to an earlier run does not affect the specified current initial state. T70B1 is read as initiating an acceleration that continues through steady rotation, giving effective gravity 13.7 m/s². The two density sentences and the two wall-height sentences preserve their respective numbers and units.
